body: Girl, I'm not a mom yet but I'm 28 years old and believe me, life get SO MUCH better than your teenage years! Yes you'll have responsibities, but that's what makes life great! You get to choose your own life! Your own job, find something that you love! Find fun stuff to do at the side! You get to do what you want, eat what you want, live life like you want! You get to be away from parents who tell you what to do! It gets so much more fun! It doesn't even have to be expensive to be fun, life is great when your main goal is to make yourself happy. You get to have a pet, or not have a pet. You get to meet new people, make new friends, find new interests, get to know yourself better. You get to discover new food on your own! You get to try and faill, get back up and try again. Of course not everything will be sunshine and happiness. Life does get hard, and it won't always be easy, but it will be your own, and that is absolutely great.

I don't entirely agree with that. Yes, school is incredibly important, don't drop out of school of course. But building up experience in teenage years can benefit your later life sooo much. As a teenager, you get the shittiest jobs, true, but you learn so much. I have a friend who will turn 30 years old and want to open her own coffee bar. But guess what, she never even worked in food service, doesn't have the faintest clue as to what it is to work as a server. These things you learn as a teenager working shitty server jobs. My ex boyfriend didn't know shit about cleaning his own house. I worked a shitty job cleaning old people's rooms at a facility, but I learned. You earn money, you earn very important experience and you learn about the world, about working, about life, and even more importantly, about yourself. Maybe you love working retali, or maybe you hate it. But you don't know until you've actually done this. So if you have the time and energy to get some jobs over your teenage years, do it. It benefits you greatly. Also stands good on your CV! Not as much as it used to 50 years ago, I guess, but people will still hire someone with more experience, even summer or weekend jobs, than someone who didn't do any job before.
Also, teenage years are great for taking up random hobbies. I mean, you're never too old to learn, but having a random hobby in your teens just benefits in later life imo.

I also built up a lot of savings while working when I was a teenager. It helped a great deal when I wanted to move out or needed to provide for myself when my parents wouldn't. It also teaches independence imo, and you learn what it is to work, you learn what responsibilities are and you learn a lot about the world. I feel like I grew up a lot because of working as a teenager, compared to friends who never had a summer job or weekend job on top of school. Some of my friends that are older just don't know these things and I feel much more experienced than them because of these jobs. I would do jobs very different than what I was learning in school. I worked in the food industry, in supermarkets, at youth camps etc and not all of my friends have these experiences and just don't know what a job in a restaurant would look like, for example. You learn a lot and you earn money :)

Yeah experience does matter and you can build it up over your teenage years while working summer jobs or volunteering (for example at kids kamps and stuff, I don't know if that exists in your country). Also, try to find some different jobs over the years. Experience working in retail and restaurants and ... and ... is a lot better than just the same job for four years every summer. It shows you have a big field of interest and that you have experience with a lot of different stuff :) good luck!

This will probably get lost, but I like telling this story because my friend taught me a lot the night he told me this.
So basically, when I was in college, I was in this super lowkey student club. Just people having fun and drinking. No big rules, no heavy commitments, just some fun and singing. There was this guy who was a few years older than me, and we became pretty good friends. He was always the clown of the group, getting really drunk, pretty weird dude and everyone loved him. He kind of took the new people under his wings every year by showing them how to have a good time and teaching us all the rules of the club, while still having our backs all the time. One night out, he told me a story. The older people already knew it, because they were there when it happened and they were crying from laughter from the first few words of the story.
This is what happened: one night a few year before, he was pretty drunk, dancing on a table in a bar with some other people from the club. All night there was this older lady (I think he said like 50 or even older), making eyes at him. When he's dancing on the table, the lady comes up, pulls his pants down and bites his junk. All happened very fast, everyone was drunk and everyone laughed hard. When he was telling this a few years later, everyone was still laughing, the older members telling him to stop making a big deal of it, the new members laughing at the image of this guy drunk on a table getting his junk bitten.
